name: Canary Mail
tagline: Build a privacy-conscious desktop email client with local indexing and optional summaries

pricing.notes: Approximate annual-equivalent Pro price; storefront pricing varies.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited email accounts; maximum 2 devices; basic email tools
tiers.notes: No Canary-imposed mailbox storage limit; storage remains governed by the email provider.

tiers.name: Growth
tiers.limits: Unlimited email accounts; maximum 5 devices; AI Copilot, full read receipts, send later, calendar/scheduling, cleaner, integrations
tiers.notes: $36/year. There is no monthly subscription; $3 is the displayed annual-plan monthly equivalent. Also sold as a lifetime purchase, whose price is shown only in-app.

tiers.name: Pro+
tiers.limits: Unlimited email accounts; maximum 5 devices; PGP, SecureSend/HIPAA, phishing/ransomware and impersonation protections
tiers.notes: $100/year. There is no monthly subscription. The page also displays $10/month in one location, which conflicts with the stated $100 annual total; this field uses the annual total divided by 12. Also sold as a lifetime purchase.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited email accounts; maximum 2 devices; no Canary-imposed storage cap
pricing.billingTerms: annual subscription or one-time lifetime purchase; no monthly plan; 7-day full-feature trial, no card and no auto-billing
pricing.hiddenCosts: Lifetime prices are shown only inside the app and are not published on the public pricing page; mailbox storage/provider charges remain outside Canary.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Canary Mail, build a privacy-conscious desktop email client with local indexing and optional summaries. The hard boundary is cross-platform clients, push, encryption features, provider support, and ai polish, plus mail infrastructure, integrations, and client polish.
coreLoopDIY: Connect an existing mailbox, index messages locally, provide a fast focused inbox with optional summaries, and send through the account's normal SMTP service.
whatYouLose: cross-platform clients, push, encryption features, provider support, and AI polish
moatNotes: mail infrastructure, integrations, and client polish
ongoingBurden: IMAP quirks, OAuth, MIME, threading, search, attachments, offline sync, notifications, secure storage, and provider changes
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Canary Mail because an email client can be rebuilt; operating a trusted mail service with excellent deliverability cannot. The recurring cost buys IMAP quirks, OAuth, MIME, threading, search, attachments, offline sync, notifications, secure storage, and provider changes, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: mailcow
priorArt.desc: Popular open-source mail-server suite that demonstrates the operational complexity of hosted mail.

alternatives.name: Apple Mail
alternatives.desc: Local indexing, tracker blocking and optional on-device summaries, provided your hardware is modern enough.

facts.install: Preinstalled on macOS, iPhone, and iPad; add an IMAP, Exchange, iCloud, Google, or other supported mailbox
facts.engines: Optional Apple Intelligence writing tools, priority-message features, and summaries on supported hardware; ordinary mail does not require an AI backend
facts.dataFormat: Messages remain in the connected mail provider and are cached or indexed in the local Mail profile; local mailboxes can be exported as mbox files
facts.gapVsPaid: Apple Mail lacks Canary’s cross-platform PGP and SecureSend workflow, and its AI summaries work only on supported Apple hardware.

alternatives.name: BlueMail Personal
alternatives.desc: Unlimited accounts, PGP and capped AI summaries for free; the privacy story is less austere than Canary's.

facts.install: Install the Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, or ChromeOS client and add existing mail accounts
facts.engines: Optional paid GemAI features use third-party large-language-model providers; the free Personal tier's core mail client does not require them
facts.dataFormat: Mail remains at the provider and is cached locally; BlueMail services may momentarily process data for push, spam protection, and optional GemAI, while some cross-device features store encrypted metadata
facts.gapVsPaid: BlueMail supports many accounts and security features, but its privacy architecture is less austere and its AI features are not a like-for-like free replacement for Canary’s Copilot.

alternatives.name: Mailspring
alternatives.desc: A local desktop index and open codebase; summaries and the privacy halo are absent.

facts.install: Install the packaged desktop app for macOS, Windows, or Linux and create a Mailspring ID
facts.dataFormat: Mail is synchronized and indexed into a local database and cache; Mailspring's service stores account and feature metadata but says it does not store message content except for features such as shared threads
facts.gapVsPaid: Mailspring has a local index but no native PGP, secure-send workflow, mobile apps, or built-in AI summaries comparable to Canary.
facts.setupBlocker: A Mailspring ID is mandatory, and there are no mobile clients

alternatives.name: Thunderbird
alternatives.desc: Private local mail and search without an account tax; AI summaries are somebody else's problem.

facts.install: Install the official Windows, macOS, or Linux package and add existing mail accounts
facts.dataFormat: Accounts, settings, indexes, address books, and locally downloaded messages live in the Thunderbird profile; message stores use mbox by default, with Maildir available, while IMAP originals remain at the provider
facts.gapVsPaid: Thunderbird handles private local mail and OpenPGP well, but it has no built-in Canary-style AI summaries or SecureSend service.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal desktop mail client DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Canary Mail in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, IMAP, SMTP, and OAuth where available; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: connect an existing mailbox, index messages locally, provide a fast focused inbox with optional summaries, and send through the account's normal SMTP service.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support one IMAP and SMTP account with credentials stored only in the OS keychain.
Index headers and message bodies locally with resumable sync and a visible status page.
Implement standards-based threading, folders, labels, archive, snooze, drafts, and search.
Render HTML email in a locked-down sandbox and block remote images by default.
Send multipart messages with attachments and preserve a local copy of every draft.
Add export, local cache reset, account reconnect, diagnostics, and safe logging.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out running a public mail server.
Deliberately leave out shared team inboxes and sales workflows.
Deliberately leave out mobile push services and provider-scale spam filtering.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
